clue.text: To irritate a worker is bold!.

parts.note: to gall someone is to irritate or vex them
the ant is the crossword's standard worker, from the worker caste of the colony

explanation.surface: An outburst: annoying an employee takes real nerve!
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' goes with 'worker' (an ant), so it adds no letter of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant can mean brave or spirited, a synonym of bold.

clue.text: A soldier turning red in rage

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters are spun around into a new order

explanation.surface: A trooper going red with fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is an infantryman, originally one who threw grenades.

clue.text: Having a cigarette amid the general greenery

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the smoke goes inside the general

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
a fag is British slang for a cigarette, so having a cigarette gives A FAG

explanation.surface: An officer lighting up among the foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is everyday British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the leaves of plants taken together.

clue.text: Soldiers, many soldiers, in Army given a rise — a change for the better

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the army word
given a rise means lifted upward, which reverses a word in a down clue

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
men are soldiers, as in officers and men
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
men again for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops, a great number of them, joining up in a promoted army as an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a rise' turns TA (Territorial Army) upward into AT, which holds MEN, D and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration meant to improve something, such as a law.

clue.text: Drink hard — like a fish

explanation.surface: Drink like a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the idiom 'drink like a fish'; 'like a' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Toping is heavy boozing, and a tope is also a kind of small shark.

clue.text: Thought like a pressman after all

indicators.note: after tells us the pressman's letters come behind the word for all

parts.note: 'as' means like, in comparisons
a sum is the whole amount, all of it
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A journalist's thinking turned out to be an assumption, when all was said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After all' reads as 'in the end', but the two words part company: 'after' is a placing signal and 'all' a word for a total.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumed, in the past tense, means supposed or believed, matching thought as a verb.

clue.text: Expertise is needed to dress in a way-out fashion

indicators.note: way-out fashion means an outlandish style, signalling letters arranged in an odd order

explanation.surface: It takes skill to dress in eccentric clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way-out fashion' looks like the dressing style; it rearranges TO DRESS IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is skill and dexterity, a synonym of expertise.

clue.text: Support a proud movement

definitions.meaning: a brace or prop in a structure
to walk in a swaggering, conceited way

explanation.surface: Backing a movement for pride.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a structural prop, and also a pompous walk.

clue.text: This island was the making of one painter

parts.note: was the making of means made someone, so made comes from the making
I is the Roman numeral one
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A painter owed his success to his time on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic.

clue.text: Stop dead very satisfactorily

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
well means satisfactorily

explanation.surface: Coming to a halt in a most pleasing manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to stay or remain somewhere, as stop does in British usage.

clue.text: Cheer up retired relation with a note

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for relation is read backwards

parts.note: a relation can be a story or account, a tale
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Lifting the spirits of a retired family member with a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' suggests a relative, but here it is a narration: a tale, read backwards by 'retired' to give ELAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with joy, which is a synonym of cheer up.

clue.text: Some hill-range where there's game

parts.note: some of a thing is a part of it
a ridge is a long line of hills

explanation.surface: A hunter's tip about the stretch of uplands where quarry can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird, shot for sport and food.

clue.text: Announcements about fighting for grants

indicators.note: about means around, so the announcements surround the fighting

parts.note: ads, short for advertisements, are announcements
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Public notices about combat being made in order to win funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Awards are sums or prizes granted, so the plural noun matches grants.

clue.text: Defective hearing

parts.note: reads as poor ears, but a hearing is also a court trial, and one that is flawed in law

explanation.surface: Someone is going deaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial declared void because of an error is a flawed court hearing.

clue.text: "Love goes towards love as — from their books" (R.and. J.)

definitions.text: Love goes towards love as — from their books

parts.words: Love goes towards love as — from their books
parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet with a word missing, the pupils who leave lessons gladly

explanation.surface: A line of Romeo's: love goes towards love as pupils run from lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: R and J is Romeo and Juliet; Romeo says love runs to love as pupils run from their lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's gap is filled by young pupils who are glad to leave their studies.

clue.text: She's from Lancashire, needless to say

definitions.note: She's is She is; the definition is She, a woman's name

indicators.note: from signals letters taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A northern woman whose county of origin goes without saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From Lancashire' looks like the woman's home, but the name runs across 'LancashIRE NEedless'; 'to say' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's given name, so it fits a clue asking for a particular she.

clue.text: Urge to study music

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a strain is a passage of music or a tune

explanation.surface: An encouragement to take up musical studies.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to force or press someone, close in sense to urge.

clue.text: Will's trial meant trouble

definitions.note: Will's reads as Will is, the definition Will with is as a link

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of meant are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's court case led to problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will's' suggests Shakespeare; it is 'Will is'. 'trouble' turns MEANT into AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a legal will, the document stating last wishes.

clue.text: Any old sweater just will not do in 'America!

definitions.text: Any old sweater just will not do in 'America!

parts.words: Any old sweater just will not do in 'America!
parts.note: reads as fashion snobbery, but splits as a fresh pullover, which names a US state

explanation.surface: Fussy about clothes in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: A jersey is a British word for a sweater; only a fresh one will do.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a state of the USA on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Tories hug honest constituents.

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the letters are reassembled from those of the words

explanation.surface: Conservatives embrace the upright voters of their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' looks like voters; it is the anagram signal working on TORIES HUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright and just, akin to honest.

clue.text: Joke about spiral descent, though plainly winded

indicators.note: about means around, so the joke goes around the descent

parts.note: a gag is a joke
a spin is an aircraft's spiralling dive

explanation.surface: A gag about a plane spinning down, leaving someone breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone breathing in gulps is visibly out of breath.

clue.text: Drive home by a roundabout way

definitions.text: Drive home by a roundabout way

parts.words: Drive home by a roundabout way
parts.note: reads as a detour on the road, but describes a fastener driven in by turning round and round

explanation.surface: Taking the long route back by car.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded fastener goes in by being twisted round, rather than hammered straight.

clue.text: Well-stocked salesman allowed a point

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
let means allowed
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A permitted salesman with plenty of goods to point at.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means full or abundantly supplied.

clue.text: Old husband incarcerated in vile prison

indicators.note: incarcerated in means locked inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: base means low or vile
to husband once meant to till or cultivate land, an archaic sense

explanation.surface: An elderly married man has been jailed in a horrible lock-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' is a verb in an archaic sense, farming the land; 'Old' warns that the sense is dated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the famous Paris fortress prison stormed in 1789.

clue.text: A youngster, a trainee, creating pandemonium

parts.note: a babe is a baby, a youngster
L is for learner, a trainee

explanation.surface: A child and a novice causing chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Babel is a scene of noisy confusion, after the biblical tower of many tongues.

clue.text: The subject of progeny

definitions.meaning: ... means offspring, as in died without ...

explanation.surface: The topic of offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means a matter under debate, and also children or descendants.

clue.text: Politician in the market for a good model

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the word for a market

parts.note: a sale is a market event where goods are sold
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP shopping around for a fine example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a representative example, as a model can be.

clue.text: Simple man mounting public transport

parts.note: he is a man

indicators.note: mounting means climbing up, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway

explanation.surface: A naive fellow boarding a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' looks like an adjective; as a noun it is an old word for a medicinal plant. BR (British Rail) goes up to give RB.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple, as a noun, is a medicinal plant, a herbal remedy.

clue.text: Yellow stuff most surprisingly found in sea-water

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so the scrambled word sits inside the water

parts.note: brine is salty sea-water

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of most have turned out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A yellow substance turning up, unexpectedly, in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' scrambles 'most' into MSTO before it goes into the salty water.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone is an old name for sulphur, a yellow element.

clue.text: It makes no odds if a woman goes to extremes

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, is the crossword's stock woman
N and S, north and south, are the extreme points of the globe, the poles

explanation.surface: A woman going over the top makes no difference.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, odds are offered against; an even-money bet has no odds either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager at evens pays exactly the stake, with no favourable or unfavourable price.

clue.text: Cannot stand having learner, say, in front of Minor

indicators.note: in front of places the first pieces before the word for minor

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
EG, for example, is signalled by say
less means minor or smaller

explanation.surface: A learner driver who is under age is unable to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: LEGLESS is British slang for so drunk one cannot stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless describes someone too intoxicated to stay on their feet.

clue.text: The torch-bearer's requirement

parts.note: suggests an Olympic runner with a flame, but means what an electric hand torch needs to shine

explanation.surface: What an Olympic flame-carrier needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric hand lamp runs on a cell of stored power.
